q: 1. The inner section of a cavity wall, is generally known as
explain: A cavity wall consists of two separate walls (leaves) with a gap between them. The inner part is called the 'inner leaf' or 'inner leaf wall'.

q: 2. The surface of the wall exposed to weather is called ...........
explain: In masonry, the 'face' is the exterior surface of a wall that is visible and exposed to the weather, while the 'back' is the inner surface.

q: 3. The portion of a brick which is cut at one corner such that at one end its width is half of that of a full brick is called ...........
explain: A king closer is formed by cutting off a triangular piece from one corner, reaching from the middle of the header to the middle of the stretcher.

q: 4. The brick which is cut such that no longer face is full and the other longer face is small in length is called ...........
explain: A mitred closer is cut at an angle (usually 45 to 60 degrees) along its length, so one stretcher face is shorter than the other.

q: 5. A groove provided on the underside of projecting elements such as cornices, copings such that rain water can be discharged clear of the wall surface is called ...........
explain: Throating is a small groove on the underside of a sill or coping that prevents rainwater from running back onto the wall, protecting it from dampness.

q: 6. Cement sand mortar preferred in load bearing wall is
explain: For load-bearing walls, a 1:6 cement-to-sand ratio provides a balanced strength that allows for minor settlements without brittle failure.

q: 7. The tool used by the masons to check the verticality of walls is ...........
explain: A plumb bob is a weighted string used to determine a perfectly vertical line (plumb) for brickwork or stone walls.

q: 8. In brick masonry, the bond produced by laying alternate headers and stretchers in each course is known as
explain: Flemish bond consists of alternate headers and stretchers in every course.

q: 9. A bonding in which all courses are laid as stretchers is known as ..........
explain: Stretcher bond (or running bond) is composed entirely of stretchers and is only used for thin walls.

q: 10. An arrangement for supporting an unsafe structure temporarily, till it is rendered safe or dismantled, is known as ..........
explain: Shoring is the use of temporary supports (shores) to stabilize a building that is in danger of collapsing or undergoing renovation.

q: 11. The compressive strength of first class and second class bricks should not be less than ..........
explain: Indian Standards typically specify that first-class bricks should have a minimum compressive strength of 105 kg/cm², but commonly 80-100 kg/cm² is cited as the safe minimum for structural work.

q: 12. The upper horizontal portion of the step where the foot is placed while ascending or descending is known as ..........
explain: The tread is the flat horizontal surface of a stair step that you walk on.

q: 13. The highest point of an arch is called
explain: The crown is the highest point of the arch, where the keystone is typically located.

q: 14. The inner curve of an arch is known as ..........
explain: The intrados is the lower or inner curve of an arch. The underside surface itself is often called the soffit.

q: 15. The portion of the wall which supports an arch is termed as ..........
explain: The abutment is the end support of an arch that resists both the vertical load and the horizontal thrust.

q: 16. Normally the rise of the steps would be between ..........
explain: A rise of 10-15 cm is standard for public buildings, while 15-18 cm is common for residential; 10-15 cm is generally safer and more comfortable.

q: 17. When the two blocks of stone have a tendency to be pulled apart in the direction of their lengths, then the type of joint to be used should be
explain: A cramped joint uses a metal 'cramp' to tie two stones together, preventing them from being pulled apart by tension.

q: 18. While laying bricks in a wall, frog of the brick must be kept
explain: The frog (indentation) is kept upward so that it fills with mortar, creating a mechanical 'key' for the course above.

q: 19. In a single day the maximum height of masonry to be raised should not be more than
explain: Masonry height is limited to 1.5m per day to prevent the fresh mortar in lower courses from being crushed by excessive weight before setting.

q: 20. To protect the top of a parapet wall from the action of rain water, it is provided with a special course and that course if known as
explain: Coping is a waterproof covering (usually stone, brick, or concrete) placed on the top of an exposed wall to shed water.

q: 21. The desired slope in Madras-terrace roofing is obtained by ..........
options: using varying thickness of brick bat concreting
using varying mortar thickness while laying flat tiles
adjusting the height of the furring piece at the centre
explain: In Madras-terrace roofs, timber furring pieces of varying heights are placed on the joists to create the necessary slope for drainage.

q: 22. The wedge shaped bricks or blocks used for the construction of an arch are called as
options: none of a, b and c
explain: Voussoirs are the tapered units that make up the curve of an arch; the center-most voussoir is specifically called the keystone.

q: 23. The exterior angle between outer faces of a wall, is known as
explain: A quoin is the external angle or corner of a building wall.

q: 24. A brick which is cut in such a way that the width of its one end is half that of a full brick, is called ..........
explain: A king closer is formed by cutting a triangular corner of the brick such that the width of one end is half the width of the brick.

q: 25. In brick masonry, for good bonding ..........
options: all bricks need not be uniform in size
bats must be used in alternate courses only
vertical joints in alternate courses should fall in plumbs
cement mortar must have surkhi as additive
explain: Proper bonding requires that vertical joints are broken (staggered) so they do not form a continuous line of weakness through the wall.

q: 26. The type of masonry in which the stones of irregular size and shapes are used and there are no regular courses, is known as ..........
explain: Uncoursed rubble masonry is the most basic form, where stones are used as they come from the quarry with minimal dressing.

q: 27. The most commonly used bond for all wall thickness is ..........
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brickwork and is the standard for most structural wall construction.

q: 28. The highest point on the extrados is called ..........
explain: The crown is the highest part of an arch, where the keystone is located.

q: 29. The vertical distance between the springing line and the highest point on the intrados is called .......... of the arch.
explain: Rise is the vertical distance from the level of the springing points to the highest point of the intrados.

q: 30. The arch consisting of fully dressed stones, is called ..........
explain: Ashlar arches use finely dressed stones with thin joints for high-quality architectural work.

q: 31. In pitched roofs, the term gable is defined as the ..........
options: apex line of the sloping roof
inclination of the sides of a roof to the horizontal plane
horizontal distance between the internal faces of the walls
triangular upper part of a wall formed at the end of a pitch roof
explain: A gable is the triangular portion of a wall between the edges of intersecting roof pitches.

q: 32. The type of masonry in which the stones of irregular size and shapes are used and there are no regular course is called ..........
explain: Random rubble masonry is the most basic and cheapest form of stone walling, using stones as they come from the quarry.

q: 33. When two blocks of stone have a tendency to be pulled apart in the direction of their lengths, then the type of joint used is called ..........
explain: A cramped joint uses a small metal 'cramp' (like a staple) to tie two stones together and resist tension.

q: 34. An external corner in brick masonry is called ..........
explain: The term quoin refers to the external corner of a wall or the stones/bricks used to form it.

q: 35. The nominal thickness of an expansion joints in brick wall must be more than ..........
explain: Expansion joints allow for thermal movement and are typically at least 20 mm wide.

q: 36. The most important tool used by a mason in laying of bricks while constructing a wall ..........
explain: The trowel is the primary tool for lifting and spreading mortar and for cutting bricks.

q: 37. Broken bricks or stone chips are also called ...........
explain: Spalls are small chips or fragments of stone or brick, often used as filling material.

q: 38. The nominal thickness of one-brick (un-plastered) wall is about ...........
explain: One-brick wall thickness is approximately 200 mm (including the mortar joint).

q: 39. The portion of wall on which the end of an arch rests is known as ...........
explain: The abutment is the masonry mass that supports the ends of an arch and resists its lateral thrust.

q: 40. Springers are those wedge shaped blocks of an arch which are provided at
explain: Springers are the first wedge-shaped units (voussoirs) placed at the ends of an arch, resting directly on the impost or the support (skewback) at the extremes.
